source_span: the long-term growth & productivity potential from the AI boom has acted as a mitigator to the various macro risks in focus today, in some sense like an 'AI put'
source_chain: AI growth narratives (Meta's Muse, mega-cap earnings/buybacks) absorb a fixed supply of investor attention, therefore macro risk (a failed 5Y auction, multi-decade-high yields, a MOVE spike above 100) gets ignored and dip-buying continues regardless of rates, therefore equities (Nasdaq +3%, new ATH) decouple from and outrun a breaking bond market. Invalidation: a slip-up in the AI narrative / a re-pricing of AI growth lower ends the attention diversion and lets the macro stress become 'real US equity risk.'
pulse_chain: Same as source: fixed attention supply -> AI narrative wins it from macro risk -> aggressive dip-buying irrespective of the bond blowup, invalidated by a downward re-pricing of AI growth expectations (explicitly named and attributed to BofA). The theme layers on a second, correctly-attributed GS/Pasquariello counter-chain (rates are a headwind not a 2022-style wrecking ball because earnings growth, not inflation, is driving the multiple compression; the 2-std-dev/50bps 'speed limit' was just triggered; Privorotsky's three-item re-risking checklist and the oil-falling-but-credit-widening observation) that matches its source notes step for step, including the $5.5bn/25bps figures.
why: Both the BofA AI-put mechanism/invalidation and the Goldman counter-argument (headwind-not-wrecking-ball, the triggered speed-of-move rule, Privorotsky's three-item checklist, the $5.5bn/25bps liquidation figures) are reproduced with correct direction and correct bank attribution; the only deviation is an unsourced 'or a credit seizure' addendum to Pasquariello's stated invalidation condition, which is additive color rather than a reversed or substituted step.
